title: An open home
hook: Abraham's tent, lived: a spare chair at the table
tomorrow: an old father told his son to turn his bookcases into what?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Avot's advice to acquire a friend, with time and food and honesty. Make a friend. Today, the house that friend walks into.
screen: `MAKE A FRIEND.` → `THE HOUSE THEY WALK INTO.`

segments.voice: The smell of something in the oven does half the welcoming before anyone says hello. Remember Sarah, laughing at the tent door? Here's the same afternoon from the front of the tent. It's the heat of the day. Abraham sits at the entrance and sees three strangers on the road. And Genesis says "he ran to meet them from the tent door." An old man, in the heat, running.
screen: `SOMETHING IN THE OVEN.` → `THE SAME AFTERNOON, FROM THE FRONT.` → `HE RAN TO MEET THEM.`

segments.voice: Look at the details Genesis keeps, and how many of them you could touch or taste. Water for dusty feet: "Let now a little water be fetched, and wash your feet." Shade: rest under the tree. Bread: Abraham hurries into the tent to ask Sarah for cakes. A tender calf, butter and milk. He offers a morsel of bread and serves a feast. Avot de-Rabbi Natan adds a detail Genesis doesn't have: Abraham's tent had openings on every side, so no traveler had to hunt for the door. Pirkei Avot turns it into a rule for every home: let your house be open wide, and let the poor be members of your household. The name for this is hachnasat orchim, bringing in guests. Notice the order. It's physical first: a seat, water, something warm. The talk comes after. So a spare chair at the table is the modern tent flap. It says, before anyone speaks, there's room for you. Something to tell a friend tonight: Abraham promised a bite of bread and then brought out a feast.
screen: `WATER, SHADE, BREAD.` · `A TENT OPEN ON EVERY SIDE.` · `LET YOUR HOUSE BE OPEN WIDE.` · `SEAT FIRST, TALK AFTER.` · then, large: `A SPARE CHAIR.`

segments.voice: If there's something to drink near you, water or tea, hold it and smell it first, then take one slow sip, the way a guest would after a long road. Notice how it lands. Then bring to mind one person who'd be glad to be offered exactly this, in a spare chair at your table.
screen: `SMELL IT FIRST.` · `ONE SLOW SIP.` · `WHO WOULD YOU OFFER THIS TO?`

segments.voice: An open home: hachnasat orchim, bringing in guests. Water, shade, bread, and a way in on every side.
For the road: a spare chair, and water offered before the questions. Day twelve, door open.

howItsDone: Hachnasat orchim is a mitzvah Jews practice by inviting guests to Shabbat and holiday meals, hosting travelers and newcomers, and at the Passover seder opening with 'let all who are hungry come and eat'.
